change: Record numeric failed-PUT status or typed transport class without changing one-attempt transport; notify existing placement on retirement without resetting failure pacing or consuming pending membership updates.

upload_diagnostics.limits: Numeric statuses describe response headers, not definitive aborts or provider root cause. Transport classes come from typed SDK errors; URLs, headers, response bodies and raw errors are not retained. A successful status followed by a decode/body error may have no boundary failure event. Recovery stages include only observed logs; cancellation/rotation may omit intervals. No timings alter authority or retry decisions.

experiments.slow_work_limits: Slow timers overlap and omit fast calls. Samples lack per-operation start offsets and database names, preventing full client-to-server causal attribution.

verification.real_http: Lost journal reply reacquires within one second, preserves exact receipts and excludes a late old-owner upload; passes in 0.17 seconds.
verification.negative_control: Disabling only the retirement notification makes the existing one-second acquisition assertion fail; mutation restored.
verification.transport: Two payload shapes across 200/301/302/303/307/308/400/403/412/429/500/503, lost replies and timeouts. One physical PUT per attempt, original error retained, sensitive sentinels excluded from diagnostics. Connection refusal remains provably unsent.
verification.membership: Retained-backend resident-budget regression verifies that retirement notifications do not consume membership updates or bypass resident permits.

tla.bounds: Three owner identities and two resident slots; retained work keeps its slot until Finish. Bounded and Funded invariants with unsafe acquisition and retirement controls; component check, not Rust refinement or complete protocol composition.

removed: Removed the normal poll delay after worker retirement while keeping polling as fallback.
Removed acknowledgement of membership changes on unrelated controller wakeups.
Reused the existing connector, controller, TCP fixture and residency model; no second transport or recovery implementation.
Restored negative-control mutations and removed generated model scratch.
limitations: No latency SLO or general throughput improvement is established. Runs differ in length, randomized placement and provider conditions.
Four HTTP 500 responses and one typed Request failure describe this run; they neither identify provider internal cause nor retroactively classify earlier failures.
Full owner recovery still takes 11.85–30.40 seconds. The longer run has an 80.52-second worst write, 25-second forwarding timeouts and preparation up to 27.71 seconds.
Two other upload failures are provably unsent; they do not retire their owners. Their specific pre-send admission cause is not identified.
Existing single-trust-domain 1.0 support scope remains unchanged.
